reason: The core claim holds and is worse than stated. Driving owner-editing at 1440, the visibility segment renders "On the plan / Kept private" and the destructive control renders "Take it off the plan" 13px below it, not 30px. Same three words, opposite meanings, adjacent controls, and the destructive one has no other label to disambiguate it, so an owner cannot tell whether it hides the item or deletes it. That is a real defect on a destructive action and no gate covers it. The vocabulary count also checks out: the row chip is "shown", its accessible name is "Shown to guests.", the section label is "What guests see", and the toggle values are "On the plan / Kept private". A reader who taps a row labelled "shown" then meets a control labelled "On the plan" is being given two vocabularies for one binary. Two sub-claims are wrong and must not travel with the fix. First, the publish note reads in full "You can turn the link off at any time. Anyone holding it then sees that it has ended.", so publish already uses "turn the link off" and the ended headline "This link has been turned off." is consistent with it, not a drift from it. Second, the "line" the finding attributes to an editing eyebrow in render-b.js is the lab caption "changing one line" in render-core.js CAPTIONS, which is showroom chrome the owner never sees, so the fix aims at the wrong file. "One thing is not going ahead" belongs to behindBlock and is already carried by this seat's admin-voice finding.
sharpenedFix: Keep only the naming work and drop the ended rewrite. In render-b.js: rename the destructive control to "Delete this moment", which is the one change that makes "the plan" stop meaning two things; change the segment values to "Shown" and "Hidden"; change the row chip text to "Shown" and its accessible name to "Shown to guests." or "Hidden from guests."; leave the section label "What guests see" as it is, since a question heading over two values is correct, not a fourth name. Then widen interaction-check.mjs line 257 from /shown|private/i to /shown|hidden/i, or the gate goes red the first time a hidden row exists. Leave the ended state alone. The proposed headline "This link has ended." drops the agent that publish promised, and cutting the footnote to "Nothing you saw before has been deleted." fails interaction-check.mjs line 441, which requires /not been deleted|not public/i and would match neither. If the caption drift is worth fixing at all, it is one word in render-core.js CAPTIONS: "changing one line" becomes "changing one moment". Note while doing it that publish uses "The moment it becomes theirs" in the temporal sense, so "moment" is carrying two meanings of its own; that is tolerable in context but do not spread the word further than the object.
